name: Tempester n°13: Voice Assign bounded when a beat is loaded
explanation: [routine] (beat header deserializer, used for every beat load) copied each pad's Voice Assign byte into [address][(beat*0x30+pad)*8] without any check. A value above 6 later indexes outside the 6-entry voice table ([address], stride 0x70) in note-on ([routine], timer-4 sequencer) and [routine], and outside the voice-select table [address]. The load now keeps the low byte, as before, and replaces any value above 6 by 0 (None, the default). The editor already limits the value to 0..6 ([routine] with the maximum at [address]). One word in place (a jump; its delay slot is unchanged) plus a 6-word stub at 0x9D07A600.

edits.why: j 0x9d07a600 ; was "lhu a0,0x0(a2)". Jump to the clamp stub; the delay slot (addu t2,ra,a1 = &[address][(beat*0x30+pad)*8]) is kept unchanged. The original store at [address] is skipped (the stub returns to [address]).
original [address]: Voice Assign word read from the beat header
andi a0,a0,0xff ; the original code stored only the low byte (sb): keep exactly that byte
sltiu t0,a0,0x7 ; t0 = 1 for 0..6 (0 = None, 1..6 = Voice 1..6, the range of the Voice Assign editor, max at [address])
movz a0,zero,t0 ; out of range (7..255) -> 0 = None, the default
j [address] ; back to the instruction after the original store
sb a0,0x80(t2) ; delay slot, original [address]: store into [address][(beat*0x30+pad)*8]
